booking_rules: Invoice in the period: Dr 1100-AR total_minor; Cr the revenue_account of each line item amount_minor. Rows carry entity_id and invoice_id, payment_id null.

Payment in the period (amount_minor > 0): Dr 1000-BANK amount_minor; for each invoice_refs allocation in the invoice currency: Cr 1100-AR with that invoice_id; any amount not covered by invoice_refs: Cr 2400-UNAPPLIED-CASH (invoice_id null).

Allocation in another currency (single reference): Cr 1950-FX-CLEARING allocation (payment currency); Dr 1950-FX-CLEARING and Cr 1100-AR the converted amount (invoice currency), all with that invoice_id.
Payment with invoice_refs = null (unidentified receipt): Dr 1000-BANK, Cr 2400-UNAPPLIED-CASH; entity_id null.
Every booked journal balances per currency; rows of one payment share payment_id.

duplicate_invoice.evidence: both invoice documents + one ledger row of each invoice's booking
duplicate_invoice.meaning: The same invoice (same entity_id, currency, total and identical line_items) is booked twice.

fx_conversion.amount: |booked invoice-currency amount - correct conversion of the applied payment-currency amount|
fx_conversion.evidence: the payment document + the fx record of the policy rate date + the ledger row with the booked invoice-currency amount; if only part of the payment was applied, also the 1950-FX-CLEARING row in payment currency that shows the applied part
fx_conversion.meaning: A cross-currency allocation was converted with a rate other than the policy rate (rate of another date, or the rate of the reverse currency pair).

payment_allocation.amount: referenced allocation minus the part applied to that invoice, in payment currency
payment_allocation.evidence: the payment document + one ledger row of that payment that shows the unapplied, partially applied or misapplied amount
payment_allocation.meaning: A payment's invoice_refs allocation was not (fully) applied to the referenced invoice: left as unapplied cash, applied only in part, or applied to a different invoice.

period_cutoff.amount: |total_minor| of the invoice or |amount_minor| of the payment
period_cutoff.evidence: the document (+ one of its ledger rows if it is booked in this ledger)
period_cutoff.meaning: A document is booked in this period although its timestamp is outside the period, or a document inside the period is missing from this period's ledger.

fx.pair: use the row with source_currency = payment currency and target_currency = invoice currency; never invert a rate
fx.publication: rates are published for every Monday-Friday date covered by fx.csv and never on Saturday or Sunday
fx.rate_date: the calendar date of the payment timestamp in the company timezone; if no rate is published for that date use the most recent earlier published date
fx.rate_definition: rate = units of target_currency per 1 unit of source_currency (major units)

matching.amount_tolerance: exact: a claimed amount matches if |claimed - expected| <= tau with tau = 0 minor units for every finding type
matching.duplicates: repeated findings are separate findings; once the issue is matched they are false positives
matching.invalid_structure: wrong value type, missing field, unknown field, more than 30 findings, more than 10 evidence ids in one finding (before de-duplication), explanation longer than 1000 code points, or an episode_id of another episode: the whole submission is invalid
matching.normalisation: none: ids, type and currency are compared as exact strings (case and whitespace matter, no aliases); affected_ids and evidence_ids are sets (order and repeats inside one list do not matter); limits are checked on the raw lists before that
matching.tie_break: maximum-cardinality matching; among maximum matchings the lexicographically smallest sequence of (reference issue id, finding index from 0) pairs, reference issues ordered by their ids in Unicode code-point order
true_positive_requires: set(evidence_ids) contains at least one complete acceptable evidence set
every evidence id is an existing public record id

period.rule: A document belongs to the period iff its timestamp (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments), compared as an instant, lies in [start, end]. Ledger rows of the period carry timestamps inside the period. Calendar dates are taken in the company timezone.

reward.f1: 2TP/(2TP+FP+FN); 1 if there are no issues and no findings; 0 if there are no issues but findings
reward.inspection_steps: all step calls before submit, including erroneous ones; submit counts toward the 100-step limit but not toward inspection_steps (all steps if the episode is truncated)
